predecessors.name: Chavda Dynasty
predecessors.text: Anahilavada (modern Patan), where Mularaja supplanted the last Chavda ruler

predecessors.name: Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty
predecessors.text: Gujarat and Kutch, the part of Cliopatria's Pratihara shape that leaves it in 942 (Pratihara dossier /ledger/27)

successors.name: Khalji dynasty
successors.text: Gujarat after Alauddin Khalji's conquest: 'In 1304, Karna lost his throne permanently after a second invasion from Delhi' (Vaghela page)

ledger.x: c. 940: Mularaja founds the Chaulukya kingdom at Anahilavada. 'Mularaja, the founder of the dynasty, supplanted the last ruler of the Chavda dynasty around 940 CE'; infobox 'Established: c. 940 CE'. The Chavda page gives 942.
942 (bridge): Gujarat and Kutch pass from the Pratihara map to the Chaulukya state.
947 (bridge): the Saurashtra part of Cliopatria's 947 shape.
947 (bridge): the Gujarat-Rajasthan border fringe leaves the Pratihara shape and enters the Chaulukya one.
By 1007: Lata passes to the Chalukyas of Kalyani.

c. 1008 (accession year): Durlabharaja takes Lata back. 'Chamundaraja's other son Durlabharaja became the next king in c. 1008 CE.... He invaded the Lata region, and defeated the Lata Chalukya ruler Kirtiraja (or Kirtipala), who was a vassal of the Kalyani Chalukyas.' The page dates his accession, not the campaign…

c. 1009 (bridge): Kirtiraja takes Lata back. 'However, Kirtiraja regained control of the region within a short time, before being defeated by the Paramara king Bhoja'. The page gives no year, so the year after 1008 is used. Added in the repair of 2026-10-19: this dossier…
By 1031 (bridge): the Paramara chiefs of Arbuda are Chaulukya vassals.
By 1074: Karna wins Lata back.
By 1077: Lata lost again, 'before losing it to one Trivikramapala within three years' of 1074.
1111 (bridge, repair of 2026-10-19): Cliopatria's 1111 shape adds the south-Rajasthan margin that paramara-dynasty /ledger/8 loses in the same year.
1111 (bridge): the Sind border.
1111 (bridge): the largest unexplained growth of the 1111 shape.
1111 (bridge): the eastern margin leaves the shape.
1135-1136: Jayasimha Siddharaja annexes Malwa.
Before 1143: the Naddula Chahamanas become Chaulukya vassals.
1142: Dhara lost.

c. 1150: Kumarapala takes Malwa from Ballala. 'The Chaulukya king Kumarapala defeated Ballala around 1150 CE. Malwa then became a province of the Chaulukyas.' The Chaulukya page: 'Kumarapala captured Malwa from Ballala, who was killed by Kumarapala's Arbuda Paramara feudatory Yashodhavala'; his empire reached 'at…
1178: the Ghurids invade the Chaulukya kingdom.

c. 1175-1178: Vindhyavarman takes Malwa back for the Paramaras. R. C. Majumdar dates the recovery to Mularaja II's reign (c. 1175-1178); A. K. Majumdar holds that 'Malwa remained under Chaulukya control during Mularaja's reign'; Dhara was Paramara 'by 1192'. Entered as the Chaulukya loss (this event is the Paramara…
1178: the Battle of Kasahrada.
1197: Aibak invades Naddula and the Naddula Chahamana line ends.
4 February 1197: Aibak takes Anahilapataka.
By 1201: the capital is Chaulukya again.

c. 1220 (bridge): the Abu Paramara line ends. Paramaras of Chandravati page: Dharavarsha 'ruled as a Chaulukya feudatory', his 'last inscription dated 1219 CE (1276 VS)', reign table 'c. 1160-1220' and 'the last known ruler of dynasty'; infobox 'Disestablished: c. 13th century CE'. The page does not say the vassalage…
1220: the Yadava Simhana invades Lata.
c. 1232: peace with the Yadavas. Seuna page: 'The Chaulukya-Yadava conflict came to end in c. 1232 with a peace treaty.'

c. 1244: Visaladeva founds the Vaghela dynasty. 'Visaladeva ascended the throne of Gujarat sometime around 1244 CE'; the Chaulukya page: 'After Tribhuvanapala, they seized the throne, establishing the Vaghela dynasty' (the Vaghelas 'had earlier served as Chaulukya generals' and claimed descent from a sister of…
1299: Alauddin Khalji's army ransacks Gujarat.
1304: the second Delhi invasion ends the contest.
1304: Gujarat goes to Delhi.
1304: the Chaulukya-Vaghela kingdom of Gujarat ends.

wars.name: Chaulukya-Paramara wars (Malwa)
wars.outcome: Jayasimha took Dhara in 1135-1136; Jayavarman I regained it 1142-1143; Ballala held it until Kumarapala's victory c.

wars.name: Ghaznavid raid on Somnath
wars.outcome: 'the Ghaznavid ruler Mahmud invaded the kingdom and raided the Somnath temple during 1024-1025 CE'; Bhima fled to Kanthkot and Mahmud 'entered the Chaulukya territory unopposed'.

wars.name: Chaulukya-Kalachuri war for Lata
wars.outcome: The Kalachuris (general Vapullaka) took Lata after Bhoja's death in 1055; Karna evicted them by 1074 and lost it to Trivikramapala within three years.

wars.name: Naddula Chahamana invasion under Karna
wars.outcome: Prithvipala 'defeated Karna', and Jojalladeva 'occupied the Chaulukya capital Anahilapataka, possibly when Karna was busy at another place'.

wars.name: Ghurid invasions of the Chaulukya kingdom
wars.outcome: Muhammad of Ghor reached Mount Abu and was beaten at Kasahrada in 1178; Aibak defeated Bhima II and sacked Anahilapataka on 4 February 1197; the capital was Chaulukya again by 1201.

wars.name: Battle of Kasahrada
wars.outcome: Chaulukya victory over Muhammad of Ghor at Kasahrada near Mount Abu; he retreated to Ghazna; no territorial change.

wars.name: Chaulukya-Chahamana war
wars.outcome: Prithviraja III 'invaded Gujarat but could not gain much success and concluded a peace treaty with Chaulukya Bhima II' (before 1187, Prithviraj page); the Chaulukya page names Jagaddeva as the negotiator.

wars.name: Yadava invasions of Lata
wars.outcome: Simhana captured Lata in 1220 and installed a vassal; peace c.

wars.name: Delhi Sultanate conquest of Gujarat
wars.outcome: Ransacked in 1299; Karna lost his throne permanently in 1304.

certainty.note: No treaty line is given on any page opened; the limits are the reach of inscriptions and of feudatories (Naddula, Jalor, Abu, Chudasama Saurashtra).
